title.ja: AgentCore: エージェントの実行環境、記憶、ツール、認証
title.en: AgentCore: A Runtime, Memory, Tools, and Identity for Agents

sources.title: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore: Overview
supports: The page lists these services by name: Harness, Runtime, Memory, Gateway, Identity, Code Interpreter, Browser, Observability, Payments, Evaluations, Optimization, Policy, Registry
Runtime is described as a secure, serverless runtime environment purpose-built for deploying and scaling dynamic AI agents and tools, with true session isolation and built-in identity
Gateway converts APIs, Lambda functions, and existing services into MCP-compatible tools and connects to pre-existing MCP servers
AgentCore offers consumption-based pricing with no upfront commitments or minimum fees
AgentCore services work together or independently with any open-source framework and with any foundation model

sources.title: AgentCore: Supported AWS Regions
supports: Asia Pacific (Tokyo) is listed as supported for harness, Runtime microVMs, Runtime Instances, Memory, Gateway, Identity, Built-in Tools, Observability, Policy, Evaluations, optimization, AWS Agent Registry and the Web Search Tool
AgentCore payments is not listed as supported in Asia Pacific (Tokyo)

sources.title: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore pricing
supports: Runtime microVMs: v1 USD 0.0895 per vCPU-hour and USD 0.00945 per GB-hour; v2 USD 0.1276 per vCPU-hour and USD 0.0169 per GB-hour (consumption)

CPU is not charged during I/O wait; billing is per second with a 1-second minimum and a 128 MB memory minimum, over the whole session from microVM ready until session termination, idle periods included
With v2, idle memory is reclaimed after 120 seconds
Gateway: USD 0.005 per 1,000 API invocations, USD 0.025 per 1,000 search invocations, USD 0.02 per 100 tools indexed per month
Identity: USD 0.010 per 1,000 tokens or API keys requested for non-AWS resources, and no additional charge when used through Runtime or Gateway

Short-term memory: USD 0.25 per 1,000 new events through 2026-10-05; from 2026-10-06 USD 1.00 per GB ingested, USD 0.20 per GB retrieved, USD 0.10 per GB-month stored, each event billed at a minimum of 12 KB
Observability is charged under Amazon CloudWatch pricing
sources.note: The page states no Region for its table. The short-term memory prices by GB have no SKU in the ap-northeast-1 Price List read the same day.

sources.title: Quotas for Amazon Bedrock AgentCore
supports: Active session workloads per account: 5,000 in us-east-1 and us-west-2, 2,500 in other Regions, adjustable
Maximum hardware allocation per session 2 vCPU / 8 GB; request timeout 15 minutes; maximum payload 100 MB; streaming maximum duration 60 minutes
Direct code deployment package: 250 MB compressed, 750 MB uncompressed; Docker image 2 GB
Data plane API request rate 1,000 TPS per account; new Runtime session creation rate 25 TPS per account
Idle session timeout 15 minutes and maximum session duration 8 hours, both adjustable through LifecycleConfiguration
Memory: 100 messages per CreateEvent, 5 CreateEvent requests per second per actor per session with conversational payloads, minimum EventExpirationDuration 7 days and maximum 365
sources.note: The CreateMemory API reference gives 3 as the minimum of eventExpiryDuration; this page says 7. The stack uses 30.

sources.title: Host agent or tools with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Runtime
supports: Each user session runs in a dedicated microVM with isolated CPU, memory, and filesystem; after session completion the microVM is terminated and memory is sanitized
Two compute types: microVMs and Instances; sessions run up to 8 hours on microVMs and up to 14 days on Instances
Works with frameworks such as LangGraph, Strands and CrewAI, and with custom agents that do not use a specific framework
A newer platform version, V2, starts the agent from a snapshot

sources.title: AgentCore Runtime: microVMs (key components, platform versions)
supports: A runtime has immutable versions; a DEFAULT endpoint is created with the runtime and follows the latest version
platformVersion is V1 or V2 and V1 is the default; V2 is available in us-east-1, us-east-2, us-west-2, eu-west-1 and ap-northeast-1
On V2 create and update take minutes and the container must report healthy within 120 seconds
AWS CloudFormation and the AWS CDK do not currently support setting platformVersion
sources.note: aws-cdk-lib 2.273.0 does declare a platformVersion property on CfnRuntime. The stack leaves it unset.

sources.title: AgentCore Runtime: HTTP protocol contract
supports: The agent listens on host 0.0.0.0, port 8080
POST /invocations takes JSON and answers JSON or text/event-stream
GET /ping answers a JSON body whose status is Healthy or HealthyBusy; while HealthyBusy the session is considered active
A 4xx or 5xx from the agent is returned to the caller as 424 RuntimeClientError
Without an Authorization header an OAuth-configured runtime answers 401 with a WWW-Authenticate header

sources.title: AgentCore Runtime service contract
supports: Supported protocols are HTTP (port 8080), MCP (port 8000, /mcp), A2A (port 9000) and AG-UI (port 8080)

sources.title: Use isolated sessions for agents
supports: AgentCore does not enforce session-to-user mappings; the client backend should maintain the relationship between users and their session IDs
A session is created on the first invoke with a runtimeSessionId provided by the application, of at least 33 characters
A session's compute stops after inactivity (default 15 minutes) or at the maximum lifetime (default 8 hours); the next invocation with the same ID provisions new compute
Data in memory or on disk persists only for the compute lifecycle; AgentCore Memory is the documented place for what must outlive it
The session header for HTTP is X-Amzn-Bedrock-AgentCore-Runtime-Session-Id

sources.title: Authenticate and authorize with Inbound Auth and Outbound Auth
supports: A runtime supports either IAM SigV4 or JWT bearer token inbound auth, not both at once
The JWT authorizer takes a discovery URL, allowed audiences, allowed clients, allowed scopes and required custom claims; allowedClients is checked against the client_id claim
The X-Amzn-Bedrock-AgentCore-Runtime-User-Id header is not verified against an authenticated identity and needs bedrock-agentcore:InvokeAgentRuntimeForUser
The Authorization header can be passed to the agent through the request header allowlist, and the agent may skip signature validation because the runtime has already validated the token
The invoke URL for a bearer token is https://bedrock-agentcore.<region>.amazonaws.com/runtimes/<escaped ARN>/invocations?qualifier=DEFAULT
Agents created on or after 2025-10-13 get workload identity permissions from a service-linked role

sources.title: Pass custom headers to Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Runtime
supports: Up to 20 headers per runtime, each value at most 4 KB
The Authorization header can be allowlisted only when the runtime has a customJWTAuthorizer; it is then validated and forwarded to the agent code

sources.title: Security best practices for AgentCore Runtime
supports: Any code running inside the microVM can obtain the execution role's credentials from the metadata service
Session-to-user mapping, input validation and prompt injection prevention are the customer's responsibility
The prompt field should be enforced to be a string, because a framework may dispatch a toolUse block found in the input
Add aws:SourceArn and aws:SourceAccount conditions to the execution role's trust policy

sources.title: IAM Permissions for AgentCore Runtime
supports: The execution role trusts bedrock-agentcore.amazonaws.com with aws:SourceAccount and aws:SourceArn conditions
The listed execution role statements include logs actions on /aws/bedrock-agentcore/runtimes/*, X-Ray actions on *, and cloudwatch:PutMetricData limited to the bedrock-agentcore namespace
sources.note: The stack omits the X-Ray statements and logs:PutResourcePolicy, because it enables neither tracing nor log delivery. Whether a runtime starts without them was not tried.

sources.title: API reference: CreateAgentRuntime
supports: agentRuntimeName matches [a-zA-Z][a-zA-Z0-9_]{0,47}
environmentVariables: at most 50 entries
requestHeaderConfiguration and platformVersion are request fields

sources.title: API reference: LifecycleConfiguration
supports: idleRuntimeSessionTimeout and maxLifetime are seconds, minimum 60 and maximum 1,209,600, defaults 900 and 28,800

sources.title: API reference: CreateMemory
supports: name and eventExpiryDuration are required; memoryStrategies is optional; eventExpiryDuration ranges from 3 to 365

sources.title: AgentCore Runtime: direct code deployment
supports: Direct code deployment packages are limited to 250 MB where container images can be up to 2 GB
With direct code deployment AWS patches the language runtime; with containers only the compute kernel

sources.title: AgentCore Runtime: direct code deployment for Node.js
supports: The entry point is a .js file that implements the /invocations POST and /ping GET endpoints; dependencies may be vendored or bundled into a single .js file with esbuild
AgentCore Runtime does not run TypeScript files natively
AgentCore Runtime only supports the arm64 instruction set architecture
ADOT instrumentation is only compatible with CommonJS module output

sources.title: Supported runtimes for code deployment
supports: Supported runtimes are Python 3.10 to 3.14 and Node.js 22 (NODE_22) on Amazon Linux 2023

sources.title: AgentCore CLI reference
supports: The CLI creates agents in Python or TypeScript, and builds a CodeZip or a Container

sources.title: npm: bedrock-agentcore (TypeScript SDK)
supports: The package bedrock-agentcore 0.4.5 describes itself as the TypeScript SDK for AWS Bedrock AgentCore, from github.com/aws/bedrock-agentcore-sdk-typescript
sources.note: Not used by this chapter's example.

sources.title: AgentCore Memory: memory types
supports: Short-term memory is the events of a session, read back with ListEvents
Long-term memory generation is an asynchronous process that runs in the background

sources.title: AgentCore Memory: terminology
supports: An event is the fundamental unit of short-term memory, organized by actorId and sessionId, immutable and timestamped

sources.title: AgentCore Memory: built-in strategies
supports: The built-in strategies are user preferences, semantic, session summaries and episodic

sources.title: AgentCore Memory: fine-grained access control through a gateway
supports: IAM controls on Memory match the IAM principal that calls Memory and cannot express a rule keyed on an OAuth or JWT identity
The documented way to bind actorId to the JWT sub claim is Memory behind a Gateway with a policy

sources.title: Service Authorization Reference: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore
supports: Condition keys bedrock-agentcore:actorId, sessionId, namespace and strategyId exist; CreateEvent and ListEvents support actorId and sessionId
CreateEvent, ListEvents, InvokeAgentRuntime and InvokeAgentRuntimeForUser are separate actions

sources.title: AgentCore Gateway: supported targets
supports: Targets are grouped as MCP targets (Lambda functions, API Gateway REST API stages, OpenAPI schemas, Smithy models, MCP servers, integration templates, connectors), HTTP targets (AgentCore Runtime, HTTP passthrough) and inference targets

sources.title: AgentCore Gateway: Lambda function targets
supports: The Lambda event is a map of the tool's input properties, and context.client_context.custom carries bedrockAgentCoreToolName, bedrockAgentCoreGatewayId, bedrockAgentCoreTargetId and message IDs
No key that identifies the end user is listed

sources.title: AgentCore Gateway: header propagation
supports: The Authorization header cannot be allowlisted on a target, and is forwarded to the target only when an interceptor Lambda provides it

sources.title: AgentCore Gateway: tool naming
supports: A tool is exposed as <target name>___<tool name>

sources.title: AgentCore Gateway: inbound authorization
supports: Inbound authorization is a JWT, an IAM identity, or offloaded (authenticate only, or no authorization)

sources.title: AgentCore Gateway: outbound authorization
supports: Lambda, API Gateway and Smithy targets support only the gateway service role (GATEWAY_IAM_ROLE) for outbound authorization

sources.title: AgentCore Identity: get a workload access token
supports: A workload access token is an AWS-signed opaque token for AgentCore's own services, such as outbound credential providers, and cannot be used for external services
GetWorkloadAccessTokenForJWT validates the token and identifies the user by its iss and sub claims; GetWorkloadAccessTokenForUserId treats the user ID as an opaque string it cannot verify

sources.title: AgentCore Identity: terminology
supports: A workload identity represents a logical application or workload; the token vault releases a credential only to the agent and user combination that obtained it

sources.title: AgentCore Observability: service-provided data
supports: Metrics are provided by default; spans and logs for an agent require explicit enablement
Viewing service-generated spans and traces needs CloudWatch Transaction Search turned on once; fuller data needs the code instrumented with the ADOT SDK

sources.title: AgentCore Observability: view data
supports: Standard output of a runtime goes to the log group /aws/bedrock-agentcore/runtimes/<agent_id>-<endpoint_name>

sources.title: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore release notes
supports: Policy and Evaluations became generally available in March 2026; AWS Agent Registry and the Instances compute type appear under August 2026; the Web Search Tool is generally available
Failure Insights is in public preview
No entry states whether platform version V2 or the Instances compute type is generally available or in preview

sources.title: AgentCore harness
supports: With harness you declare the model, tools, skills and instructions, and AgentCore runs the loop in an isolated microVM per session, backed by AgentCore Runtime
Harness is powered by Strands Agents and has no separate charge

sources.title: AgentCore harness: tools
supports: Tool types are remote_mcp, agentcore_gateway, agentcore_browser, agentcore_code_interpreter and inline_function; an inline function runs on the client side while the harness pauses

sources.title: AgentCore harness: operations
supports: maxIterations defaults to 75 and timeoutSeconds to 3600; maxTokens has no default

sources.title: What's New: AgentCore harness is generally available

sources.title: Cloudflare Agents

sources.title: Cloudflare Agents: what are agents
supports: Each agent instance has its own SQLite database; agents sleep when idle and wake on demand

sources.title: Cloudflare Agents: limits

sources.title: Cloudflare Durable Objects pricing

sources.title: Cloudflare Sandbox SDK

sources.note: The page does not state whether the Sandbox SDK as a whole is generally available.

sources.title: AI SDK: agents overview
supports: The AI SDK describes agents as models that use tools in a loop, and provides a ToolLoopAgent class with stopWhen and prepareStep for loop control

sources.title: Vercel Sandbox
supports: Vercel Sandbox runs untrusted or agent-generated code in isolated Firecracker microVMs, each with its own filesystem and network

sources.title: Vercel Sandbox pricing
supports: Active CPU USD 0.128 per hour and memory USD 0.0212 per GB-hour; time spent waiting for I/O does not count toward Active CPU; sessions last up to 45 minutes on Hobby and 24 hours on Pro and Enterprise

sources.title: Vercel Workflow
supports: Workflow runs multi-step logic as durable code that can retry failed steps, wait for external events, and resume across crashes and deployments

definition.ja: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore のうち、エージェントのコードを預かって動かす部分。セッションごとに専用の microVM を用意し、`/invocations` と `/ping` を持つ HTTP サーバーとしてコードを呼ぶ。
definition.en: The part of Amazon Bedrock AgentCore that hosts an agent's code. It gives each session a microVM of its own and calls the code as an HTTP server with `/invocations` and `/ping`.

glossary.ja: ランタイムセッション

definition.ja: AgentCore Runtime が 1 つの microVM に割り当てる単位。呼び出す側が決めた 33 文字以上の ID で区別される。ID がだれのものかを AgentCore は確かめない。
definition.en: The unit AgentCore Runtime gives one microVM to, told apart by an ID of 33 characters or more that the caller chooses. AgentCore does not check whose ID it is.

definition.ja: エージェントの記憶を預かる AgentCore のサービス。短期記憶は actor とセッションごとのイベントの列で、長期記憶はそこから非同期に取り出したレコード。
definition.en: The AgentCore service that keeps an agent's memory. Short-term memory is a list of events per actor and session; long-term memory is records extracted from them asynchronously.

note.ja: 8 ファイル、51 件。HTTP の約束（/ping と /invocations）、文字列でないプロンプトや余分なキーの拒否、転送されたトークンからの利用者の読み取り（署名を検査しないことの固定を含む）、ほかの利用者のセッション ID の拒否（同じプロセスでも入れ替わったプロセスでも）、ノートの指示に従うモデルに対する不変条件、記憶の畳み込み（重複、欠け、順不同）、ストアが書き込みを断ったとき・同時に終わったとき・プロセスが入れ替わったときの一致、Memory のイベントとの対応、スタックのアサーション
note.en: 8 files, 51 tests. The HTTP contract (/ping and /invocations), refusal of a prompt that is not a string and of extra keys, reading the user from a forwarded token (pinning that the signature is not checked), refusal of another user's session ID in the same process and in a replaced one, the invariant against a model that obeys a note, folding memory (duplicates, holes, any order), agreement of process and store when the store refuses a write, when two answers finish together, and when the process is replaced, the mapping to Memory events, and stack assertions

summary.ja: 50章のスタックを AWS に一度もデプロイしていない。cdkd 0.296.28 が `AWS::BedrockAgentCore::Runtime`（`RequestHeaderConfiguration` を持つので Cloud Control API 経由）と `AWS::BedrockAgentCore::Memory` を作れること、direct code deployment の ZIP を cdkd のアセットとして置けて実行ロールが読めること、CommonJS の `app.js` が Node.js 22 で起動すること、X-Ray と `logs:PutResourcePolicy` を省いた実行ロールで足りること、MMDSv2 の既定（`CfnRuntime` に property が無い）が未確認。
summary.en: The chapter 50 stack has never been deployed. Unverified: that cdkd 0.296.28 creates `AWS::BedrockAgentCore::Runtime` (through Cloud Control API, because it carries `RequestHeaderConfiguration`) and `AWS::BedrockAgentCore::Memory`, that the direct code deployment ZIP can be placed as a cdkd asset and read by the execution role, that the CommonJS `app.js` starts on Node.js 22, that the execution role is enough without the X-Ray statements and `logs:PutResourcePolicy`, and what MMDSv2 defaults to (`CfnRuntime` has no property for it).

resume.ja: `vp run agentcore:infra:deploy` のあと、deploy のページの手順で利用者とトークンを作り、`AIH_ACCESS_TOKEN=... vp run agentcore:invoke`、`vp run agentcore:infra:drift` を通す。呼び出しが `ValidationException` なら `metadataConfiguration.requireMMDSV2` を疑う。終わったら `vp run agentcore:infra:destroy` と、`/aws/bedrock-agentcore/runtimes/` で始まるロググループの削除。
resume.en: After `vp run agentcore:infra:deploy`, create a user and a token as the deploy page describes, then run `AIH_ACCESS_TOKEN=... vp run agentcore:invoke` and `vp run agentcore:infra:drift`. If an invocation answers `ValidationException`, suspect `metadataConfiguration.requireMMDSV2`. Finish with `vp run agentcore:infra:destroy` and delete the log groups that start with `/aws/bedrock-agentcore/runtimes/`.

summary.ja: Runtime がエージェントに渡すリクエストの形を実機で見ていない。許可リストに入れた `Authorization` がその名前で届くこと、`X-Amzn-Bedrock-AgentCore-Runtime-Session-Id` が届くこと、server-sent events がそのまま流れること、エージェントの 4xx が 424 になること、microVM の中で AWS SDK が設定なしに実行ロールの認証情報を見つけること、`AdminInitiateAuth` で取った Cognito のアクセストークンが `allowedClients` の検査を通ることが未確認。
summary.en: The request the Runtime hands the agent was never observed. Unverified: that an allowlisted `Authorization` arrives under that name, that `X-Amzn-Bedrock-AgentCore-Runtime-Session-Id` arrives, that server-sent events flow through as they are, that the agent's 4xx becomes 424, that the AWS SDK finds the execution role's credentials inside the microVM with no configuration, and that a Cognito access token from `AdminInitiateAuth` passes the `allowedClients` check.

resume.ja: デプロイしたうえで `vp run agentcore:invoke` を実行し、エージェントのロググループで `invocation` の行と `owner` を確かめる。届かないヘッダーがあれば、一時的に `LOG_LEVEL=debug` でヘッダー名だけを出して調べる（トークンの値は出さない）。
resume.en: Deploy, run `vp run agentcore:invoke`, and check the `invocation` lines and their `owner` in the agent's log group. If a header does not arrive, log header names only for a while with `LOG_LEVEL=debug` (never the token's value).

summary.ja: AgentCore Memory を呼んでいない。`CreateEvent` がこの章のペイロード（会話 2 件とメタデータ `seq`）を受け付けること、`clientToken` の重複が無視されること、`ListEvents` が返す形、Cognito の `sub` とこの章のセッション ID（16 進 32 桁、ハイフン、UUID）を `actorId` と `sessionId` として受け付けること、短期記憶の東京の単価が未確認。API リファレンスは `eventExpiryDuration` の下限を 3、クォータのページは 7 と書いている（スタックは 30）。
summary.en: AgentCore Memory was never called. Unverified: that `CreateEvent` accepts this chapter's payload (two conversational items and a `seq` metadata value), that a repeated `clientToken` is ignored, the shape `ListEvents` returns, that a Cognito `sub` and this chapter's session ID (32 hex digits, a hyphen, a UUID) are accepted as `actorId` and `sessionId`, and the Tokyo price of short-term memory. The API reference gives 3 as the minimum of `eventExpiryDuration` and the quotas page 7 (the stack uses 30).

resume.ja: デプロイ後、同じセッションで 2 問聞いて 2 問目が 1 問目を踏まえること、5 分以上あけてからも踏まえることを確かめる。`aws bedrock-agentcore list-events` でイベントの形を見て `src/memory-events.ts` のスキーマと比べる。請求書か Cost Explorer で短期記憶の項目と単価を確かめ、`data/fragments/50.json` に単価を足す。
resume.en: After deploying, ask two questions in one session and check that the second builds on the first, and still does after a pause of more than 5 minutes. Look at the events with `aws bedrock-agentcore list-events` and compare them with the schema in `src/memory-events.ts`. Read the short-term memory line item and rate from the bill or Cost Explorer, and add the price to `data/fragments/50.json`.

summary.ja: Runtime の Instances とプラットフォームバージョン V2 が一般提供かプレビューかを書いた一次情報を見つけられなかった。ドキュメントは CloudFormation と CDK が `platformVersion` に未対応と書くが、`aws-cdk-lib` 2.273.0 の `CfnRuntime` には property がある。
summary.en: No primary source was found that says whether the Runtime's Instances compute type and platform version V2 are generally available or in preview. The documentation says CloudFormation and the CDK do not support `platformVersion`, while `CfnRuntime` in `aws-cdk-lib` 2.273.0 has the property.

resume.ja: リリースノートと What's New を読み直す。V2 を試すなら、`platformVersion: "V2"` を足して synth し、Cloud Control API が受け付けるかをデプロイで確かめる（作成に数分かかり、120 秒以内に `/ping` が Healthy を返す必要がある）。
resume.en: Read the release notes and What's New again. To try V2, add `platformVersion: "V2"`, synth, and let a deployment show whether Cloud Control API accepts it (creation takes minutes, and `/ping` must answer Healthy within 120 seconds).
